lots.guide_summary: Close entries only: one SOLD (Gowans spelter-mounted ewer pair, $40 hammer, Oct 2025) and one ASKING (Chairish pair, US$339, about A$487). No UNSOLD. Everything else is category guidance: decorative pairs at Gowans sold $20 to $380 hammer in the last 12 months (plain or damaged $20 to $75, good gilt or hand painted $155 to $190, finer garnitures $300 to $380); filler: Galileo thermometer $20, barometers $30 to $40. USD at A$1.437.
lots.working: No SOLD entry is the same item (an ivory and pale blue raised-gilt ewer pair) in similar condition, so keep and flip maximums are both 0 under the rules. For context only: category pairs suggest the ewers alone would resell around $60 to $150 hammer if sound; the filler perhaps $50 to $90.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark read (bases not photographed), condition unknown (AS IS), and no same-item sale; evidence is category SOLD plus one US asking price.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 confirms the pair: fluted gilt-lined blue shoulders, raised gilt bird on a bramble branch with berries on ivory bodies, gilt scroll handles, square blue plinth feet with gilt edging rubbed on the corners. Ivory glaze slightly speckled. No cracks or chips visible at this resolution but bases and inside rims not shown. Photo 3 a Galileo thermometer in a black frame; photo 4 a modern light oak banjo barometer with thermometer, a petit-point dial desk clock in a brass arched frame and a heavily tarnished plated oval tray.
lots.condition: Ewers look intact in the photos with gilt wear on the plinth edges; the AS IS title means faults not shown are possible. Filler looks used but complete; tray badly tarnished.
lots.question_for_armitage: Why is the lot marked AS IS: are the ewers cracked, chipped or restored (handles, spout rims, plinth feet)? Is there any mark on the ewer bases (Royal Worcester, Hadley, a registration number or a Continental mark), and do the clock and barometer work?
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all 14 Gowans records re-opened via the API and titles, prices and bid counts match. Reclassified: Gowans 379355 (green jugs) and 390468 (majolica jugs) moved from close to category guide, as they are different items. Snippet-only UK results in the researcher's notes (Bonhams, Shapiro, Tooveys, Fellows) were never entries and remain unused.

lots.working: keep: lowest same-item SOLD = Gowans tin $105 (Kerleys $30 is too small a quantity to count as similar, so filed close). 105 / 1.22 = 86.07, rounded down to $85. flip: likely resale about $105 hammer on the Gowans evidence (lot 443 is larger, but album sets at $25 to $40 show demand is thin, so no uplift assumed); less an assumed 15% vendor commission = $89.25, no postage (local auction resale); 89.25 / 2.44 = 36.6, rounded down to $35.
lots.confidence_reason: Series confirmed from the bundle labels and card fronts, with one same-item SOLD in the Tasmanian room and one close loose-card SOLD, both opened; the card count is only an estimate and variety premiums are unproven.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: painted wading birds and ducks on rounded-corner cards, matching the Tuckfields 289-384 water bird run. Photos 3 to 7: labels read 'Series Birds Thin/Brown Set E' 1-96, 97-192, 193-288, 289-384; 'Studies Dark Brown print C'; 'Bird Studies Grey D'; 'Coppertone' 97-192, 193-288, 289-384; 'SB Thick' and 'SB Thicker'; set F bundles, some marked Complete; one note 'Spare Coppertone lighter brown'. Photo 1 shows four boxes, roughly 60 bundles visible.
lots.condition: Cards look clean with light edge toning; stored in paper bands with rubber bands, which can mark cards. Completeness of each run not verifiable from photos.
lots.question_for_armitage: Roughly how many cards or bundles are in the lot, are all four boxes included, and are the runs marked Complete actually complete? Any rubber band damage or albums included?
